games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence is written as an imperative instruction?
choices: The hands are washed by me.
I washed my hands before dinner.
Wash your hands before you eat.
rounds.answer: Wash your hands before you eat.
rounds.explanation: An imperative starts with the base verb and needs no subject, so only the last sentence gives an instruction.

rounds.prompt: Read this line from “The Attic Clue”: “It had buttons and even a tiny _____ made of plastic.” Which word fits the gap?
rounds.explanation: The toy helicopter's shield was the flat guard that protected its wires from harm.

rounds.prompt: Which word completes the safety rule from the microwave talk: “Stir the food with a clean _____ before you eat.”?
rounds.explanation: The talk asks you to stir with a clean utensil, and a spoon or fork is exactly that.

games.title: Question Quest
games.description: Read each unit question carefully and choose the best answer.

rounds.prompt: In “A Look at the Stars”, what can a telescope show you on the moon?
rounds.explanation: The text says you can see the craters on the moon and the rings around a planet.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses “have to” correctly?
choices: She have to clean the attic.
She has to clean the attic.
She has to cleaning the attic.
She have to cleaning the attic.
rounds.answer: She has to clean the attic.
rounds.explanation: After she we use has to, and the verb that follows stays in its base form: clean.

rounds.prompt: Which word correctly completes this sentence: “A crew is a group of people _____ work together.”?
rounds.explanation: We use who for people; which is for things, whose shows belonging and what is not a relative pronoun here.

games.title: Unit Mission
games.description: Finish with a mixed challenge across the whole unit.

rounds.prompt: Which machine would you use to heat a bowl of soup quickly?
rounds.explanation: A microwave is a machine that cooks or heats food quickly, so the soup is warm in minutes.

rounds.prompt: Which word names big machines that work together to do a heavy job?
rounds.explanation: Machinery names the big machines; cocoa is a powder, an attic is a room and a crew is a group of people.

rounds.prompt: Read this line from “The Attic Clue”: “They took flashlights, brooms, and a _____ to hold any papers they found.” Which word fits the gap?
rounds.explanation: Only a folder holds papers; the other three are vehicles or a viewing tool.
